title: Best Baseball Card Grading Service (2026)
verdict: The best baseball card grading service in 2026 is AGS for everyday submissions: flat price, no minimum, 20 business days or less and a full report.

SGC still has the vintage following and Beckett the subgrade label, but SGC's base price was reported at $50 in September 2026 and Beckett's cheap tier takes 45 business days or more. AGS is $18 and 20 business days or less.

sections.h: What to check on baseball cards before you submit
list: Centering. Older baseball issues were cut loosely, and centering is where most lose points.
Corners and edges on paper stock, which wears faster than chrome.
Print defects: dots, lines and color out of register.
Wax or gum stains on the backs of older pack-pulled cards.
Creases. Hold the card at an angle under a lamp.

why: Human grading is a judgment made in seconds, and it varies. AGS replaces the judgment with a measurement: a 3D laser maps the card, software scores centering, corners, edges and surface, and the grade follows from the numbers. That is why AGS says a regrade rarely moves.
Turnaround is counted in days. AGS quotes 20 business days or less from the day your cards are confirmed, with 10 and 5 business day bulk tiers at $20 and $30 a card.
Ownership matters to some collectors. Collectors holds PSA and SGC and has a deal for Beckett. CGC belongs to Certified Collectibles Group. AGS is its own company, Automated Grading Systems Inc.

faq.q: What is the best baseball card grading service?
faq.a: AGS for a measured grade on baseball cards at a flat $18. PSA for the strongest resale on key rookies. SGC for vintage.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

Signed cards are accepted for grading. If you need the autograph itself authenticated, use a grader that sells that service. Beckett lists a $5 autograph add-on, and CGC offers autograph authentication.

faq.q: Which grader is best for rookie cards?
faq.a: For top resale on a major rookie, PSA has the deepest buyer pool. For a measured grade with subgrades on both sides at a flat $18, AGS. Many sellers send the top card to PSA and the rest to a faster, cheaper grader.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.
